podcast.body: Initially released as R.E.M.'s first single before their debut album, it was later re-recorded and included on *Murmur*. The original version featured Michael Stipe's vocals without defined lyrics; he would instead murmur, babble, and play with his voice, treating it as an expressive instrument rather than delivering concrete words. "la primer single de Rem el Radio Free Europe que sacaron antes del primer disco, que luego tenía incluido lo volverían a grabar en el murmur, no tenía letra definida."

podcast.body: R.E.M.'s first record was a 7-inch single titled "Radio Free Europe," released one year and ten days after their initial performance at the church on Okeney Street in Athens. This original version was a foundational piece in their discography. "They called the song Radio Free Europe."

podcast.body: This is a re-edited classic single from the band's early discography, released on a 12-inch record. The speaker notes it's an annual tradition for R.E.M. to re-edit a classic single, often on beautiful colored vinyl. "todos los años ER no reedita un single clásico de la primera parte de su discografía."

podcast.body: This was R.E.M.'s first record, a seven-inch single made one year and ten days after their initial party performance at the church on Okeney Street in Athens. The original version is described as rootsy, made-in-America, anti-synthesizer guitar pop that stood out from the British new wave dominating new rock in the early 1980s. "REM's first record was a seven-inch single made one year and ten days after they played that party at the church on Okeney Street in Athens. They called the song Radio Free Europe. Here's the original."
